extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists, serious readers, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on recognising, shaping, and judging the form and subject of the novel; emphasizes unity of subject and form, control of scale, point of view, and avoidance of irrelevant intrusions. Aimed at people who write novels or read them critically to learn craft principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and use the various forms of narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: They are the various forms of narrative, the forms in which a story may be told; and while they are many, they are not indeed so very many... to use them is easier than to perceive their demands and their qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and read critically the books in which they appear; use the different narrative forms consciously and questioningly in order to discern their demands and qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study methods of novelists with incontestable effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us very carefully follow the methods of the novelists whose effects are incontestable, noticing exactly the manner in which the scenes and figures in their books are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pause over scenes and figures to see by what arts and devices an episode is given relief or a character made intelligible and vivid; these observations yield discoveries about the making of a novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and use a precise critical vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: The refinements of the art of fiction have been accepted without question... The expressions and the phrases at our disposal bear no defined, delimited meanings; they have not been rounded and hardened by passing constantly from one critic’s hand to another’s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of loose terms ('dramatic', 'pictorial', 'scenic', 'generalized') and strive for a received nomenclature or precise definitions when analysing structure and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the novel as art; do not be shy about analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not a piece of life, it is a piece of art like another; the fact that it is an ideal shape ... makes it all the more important that in our thought it should be protected by no romantic scruple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticise without undue delicacy—analysis will not destroy the work; approach the book as an artistic object whose parts can be examined and judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin with a clear subject; the novelist’s eye for subject is cardinal
rubrics_metrics.description: How a novelist finds his subject ... is beyond us; the power that recognizes the fruitful idea is a thing apart. For this reason we judge the novelist’s eye for a subject to be his cardinal gift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While discovery of subject may be instinctive, once announced the subject should guide treatment; readers and critics should locate and follow the subject to understand the logic of the author's course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the treatment aligned with the heart of the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this proceeding of the author the right one, the best for the subject? Is it possible to conceive and to name a better? ... We find that we are creating a design, large or small, simple or intricate, as the chapter finished is fitted into its place; or again there is a flaw and a break in the development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the author's choices start from and develop the core of the subject, or whether they diverge, contradict, or disregard it; identify flaws and breaks in development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge the whole design after finishing; form must express the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: If the form is to the eye imperfect, it means that the subject is somehow and somewhere imperfectly expressed, it means that the story has suffered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the book is complete, evaluate whether its form is coherent and whether it faithfully expresses and exhausts its subject; locate where and why the expression fails if it does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure unity: form and subject should coincide
rubrics_metrics.description: The best form is that which makes the most of its subject — there is no other definition of the meaning of form in fiction. The well-made book is the book in which the subject and the form coincide and are indistinguishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a form that uses all the matter in service of the subject; avoid surplus material or missing elements so the form and subject become one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject must be expressible succinctly (unity in a phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the novelist’s intention, in a phrase? If it cannot be put into a phrase it is no subject for a novel; and the size or the complexity of a subject is in no way limited by that assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before shaping a novel, be able to state its unifying intention concisely; this concise subject will determine and support the form of the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixing two large themes or designs
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a confusion of two designs ... It has no centre, and Tolstoy is so clearly unconcerned by the lack that one must conclude he never perceived it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let two independent and large themes run concurrently such that neither is subordinated or unified; two 'novels' in one work undermines centre and cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control scale: balance panoramic scope with detailed scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a panoramic vision of people and places ... he spreads further than any one else, but he also touches the detail of the scene ... with exquisite lightness and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large, crowded novels, plan composition so the broad panorama and fine detail both serve the central design; maintain a clear sense of direction and centre despite ample scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical or epic material to serve the central story, not overwhelm it
rubrics_metrics.description: The historic scene is used as a foil and a background ... it appears from time to time, for the sake of its value in throwing the nearer movement of life into strong relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating public/historical episodes, ensure they illuminate the novel's primary subject (e.g., personal lives) rather than displacing it by becoming the dominant focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid didactic authorial intrusions and pamphleteering
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolstoy is capable of thrusting into his book interminable chapters of comment and explanation, chapters in the manner of a controversial pamphlet, lest the argument of his drama should be missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interrupt narrative flow with prolonged authorial exposition or polemic; such intrusions may cause readers to skip pages and break the novel’s momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose and maintain a coherent point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: He approaches it through the mind of an onlooker, borrowing the value of indirectness ... But he chooses his onlooker at random and follows no consistent method. The predominant point of view is simply his own, that of the independent story-teller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select narratorial stance or onlooker deliberately and apply it consistently; random shifts of vantage weaken the unity and alter the principle governing different parts of the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape scenes and figures so they provide relief and vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: The scenes and figures, as I have said, we shape, we detach ... to see by what arts and devices ... this episode has been given relief, that character made intelligible and vivid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing episodes, use devices that give them relief and make characters intelligible and vivid—study exemplary instances and emulate their techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wastefulness: fully develop chosen story and avoid irrelevant imports
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolstoy’s novel is wasteful of its subject; that is the whole objection to its loose, unstructural form. Criticism bases its conclusion upon nothing whatever but the injury done to the story, the loss of its full potential value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all material is instrumental to the subject; do not import secondary or irrelevant narratives that dilute or fragment the main story, and develop the chosen theme to its full potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size or complexity never excuses lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be the simplest anecdote or the most elaborate concatenation of events ... it is anyhow expressible in ten words that reveal its unity. The form of the book depends on it, and until it is known there is nothing to be said of the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of novel length or ambition, insist on a unifying idea that governs structure; plan form from that unity rather than allowing size to substitute for coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical readers should relate scenes back to the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: From point to point we follow the writer, always looking back to the subject itself in order to understand the logic of the course he pursues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a reader or critic, continually test episodes and authorial choices against the declared or discovered subject to judge whether they further or detract from the novel’s design.
